collection_summary: This instance is a source-defined ground truth listing the 13 numbered permanent NATO Secretaries General with completed terms 1952-2024 (excluding incumbent Mark Rutte and 3 acting SG rows: Sergio Balanzino x2 + Alessandro Minuto-Rizzo x1, all marked with '–' rather than numbered officeholder rows in the master table). For each SG the staged row records the Term Start Year, Term End Year, and the SG's birth country derived from the per-person Wikipedia article's 'Born' field using the modern-sovereign-country-of-birthplace normalization rule. The schema is designed for implicit_join benchmark evaluation: Secretary-General + Term Start Year + Term End Year are directly from the master NATO article; Birth Country is the implicit-join cell requiring per-person Wikipedia article lookup. IMPORTANT: Birth Country is the modern sovereign country containing the birthplace, NOT the SG's nationality or country of political career — Hastings Ismay was born in British India (1887) so his Birth Country = India (modern country), not United Kingdom (his career country). claim_type = source_defined because the row universe is the master table's numbered permanent officeholder rows filtered by 'term_end_year IS NOT NULL' (mechanical incumbent-exclusion filter).
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (Secretary_General_of_NATO): master article supplying universe + filter + 3 of 4 cells per row. The NATO master article's officeholders table contains numbered rows for permanent SGs and '–'-marked rows for acting SGs; the staged universe is the numbered permanent rows with completed terms (incumbent Rutte excluded; 3 acting SG rows excluded). Term Start Year and Term End Year are integer years extracted from the master table's full-date entries.
- source_urls[1-13] (13 per-person Wikipedia articles): per-person source supplying Birth Country (the implicit-join cell). Each SG's Wikipedia article 'Born' field names the birthplace; modern-sovereign-country normalization rule applied (Ismay born Naini Tal, British India → 'India' modern country, NOT 'United Kingdom' nationality/career country).

Multi-source Tier B instance (source_count = 14 = 1 master + 13 per-person articles). The 13 per-person articles cover all 13 distinct SGs (each SG had one continuous term so no per-person article re-use). Cell-level audit: Secretary-General / Term Start Year / Term End Year cells can be spot-checked against the master NATO officeholders table; Birth Country can be spot-checked against the per-person article's 'Born' field with the modern-sovereign-country normalization applied.

Implicit-join structure: master NATO article gives (Secretary-General, Term Start Year, Term End Year); per-person Wikipedia articles supply Birth Country — a clean single-master-multiple-per-entity implicit join matching the parallel-Booker / parallel-Pulitzer / nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals / notable_works_of_recent_nobel_literature_laureates / landmark_us_supreme_court_decisions_by_chief_justice precedents. CRITICAL DESIGN POINT: Birth Country is intentionally distinct from the master NATO table's 'Country of origin' column (which would give nationality / political-career country) — the implicit join is non-redundant because Birth Country requires per-person article lookup. Ismay-India is the most-visible audit case demonstrating this distinction (career country UK; birth country India).
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass (after pre-staging audit design review — see post-staging cycle-0 notes below). Universe (13 numbered permanent NATO SGs with completed terms 1952-2024) is fully source-defined via the master NATO Secretary General Wikipedia article's officeholders table filtered to numbered-permanent-rows with completed terms. Per-row attribute cells are verbatim from the master (Secretary-General + Term Start + Term End) or grounded by per-person articles (Birth Country). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical recent SGs (Stoltenberg, Rasmussen, Solana); mid-difficulty cells include the Cold War / post-Cold War SGs (Carrington, Wörner, Claes); harder calibration cells include the early Cold War SGs (Ismay, Spaak, Stikker, Brosio, Luns) and the Ismay-India edge case. Row count (13) clears the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected to saturate implicit_join at 8/8 with a non-literary-award angle for diversity over the recent Booker + Pulitzer literary-award precedents.
- Category: implicit_join (gap 1 before this staging — `implicit_join` at 7 of 8 with nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals, notable_works_of_recent_nobel_literature_laureates, landmark_us_supreme_court_decisions_by_chief_justice, booker_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024, pulitzer_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024, and 2 registered trial_join_*; this instance brings implicit_join to 8 of 8 — SATURATES the category, NINTH category to fully clear after multi_attribute_projection, set_operation, set_filter, causal, factual_lookup, top_k, multi_hop, qualitative).
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, multi-source; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 14 (1 master + 13 per-person articles).
- Expected shape: 13 rows × 4 columns; single PK = Secretary-General.
- Domain: Politics/International Relations — extends the existing Politics/International Relations subdomain from 1 instance (nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals) to 2 instances. Per the parallel-NATO precedent, this subdomain is appropriate for NATO-keyed instances.
- Entity class: people/diplomats — NEW fine-class within the people bucket (people bucket currently has 10 fine-classes; this instance adds diplomats as the 11th — NATO Secretaries General are international diplomats per the Wikipedia article's framing).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Incumbent exclusion (Rutte) is a mechanical filter (Term End Year IS NOT NULL); audit confirmed this preserves claim_type=source_defined. (b) 3 acting SG rows excluded per the master table's '–' marker distinguishing acting from numbered permanent (Balanzino x2 in 1994/1995; Minuto-Rizzo x1 in 2003-2004). (c) Birth Country uses modern-sovereign-country normalization: Ismay = India (born British India), NOT United Kingdom (career country); Wörner = Germany (born Stuttgart, Germany per his Wikipedia article's Born field). (d) Name normalization uses per-person Wikipedia article titles per audit recommendation: 'Hastings Ismay, 1st Baron Ismay' / 'Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington' / 'George Robertson, Baron Robertson of Port Ellen' preserve peerage titles per article-canonical form rather than shortened display names ('Lord Ismay' / 'Lord Carrington' / 'George Robertson'). (e) Stoltenberg's Term End Year is 2024 (his tenure was extended from original 2022 end date due to Russia-Ukraine geopolitical context; the article-stated end date '1 October 2024' is the staged value). (f) operation_type = 'join' per protocol's canonical vocabulary (lesson pre-applied from Booker/Pulitzer cycle-1 BLOCKINGs).
- Decision: Stage.

Pre-staging audit design review (2026-05-16): audit agent confirmed the design is basically sound with 2 required fixes applied in cycle-0 staging: (1) Acting SG exclusion must include ALL 3 acting rows (Sergio Balanzino x2 + Alessandro Minuto-Rizzo x1), not just Balanzino as initially proposed; the master table marks acting rows with '–' rather than numbered officeholder rows, providing a clean mechanical filter. (2) Name normalization uses per-person Wikipedia article titles ('Hastings Ismay, 1st Baron Ismay' not 'Hastings Ismay' or 'Lord Ismay'; 'Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington' not 'Lord Carrington'; 'George Robertson, Baron Robertson of Port Ellen' not 'George Robertson') for exact-provenance per the audit-recommended rule. Audit also confirmed: (i) Birth Country = modern sovereign country (Ismay = India per Born-field rule), (ii) entity class people/diplomats (NEW fine-class) is more appropriate than people/politicians for NATO SGs, (iii) Term End Year integer column is preferable over Tenure text cell (Tenure-text loses integer evaluability), (iv) source_count=14 is appropriate (1 master + 13 per-person), (v) claim_type=source_defined is acceptable when the row filter is stated as 'numbered permanent SG row AND term_end_year IS NOT NULL'.

Post-audit (2026-05-16, cycle 1): cycle-1 audit verdict 'Ready with residual hygiene' — 0 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Data-level checks all passed (13 rows × 4 cols; PK unique; chronological term ordering; source_count=14=len(source_urls); operation_type=join; all 13 birth-country cells grounded by per-person Born fields). The single hygiene item bundled 3 prose-drift accuracy issues in current-state prose (CSV cells remain correct): (a) Minuto-Rizzo / de Hoop Scheffer handover prose said '5 January 2004' but master NATO table says '1 January 2004'; (b) Ismay term-start example prose said '4 April 1952' but master table says '24 March 1952'; (c) Wörner birthplace prose used 'Weimar Republic / Württemberg territory (1934)' framing despite the per-person Wikipedia article's Born field saying simply 'Stuttgart, Germany'. Resolved by: (i) draft.json::temporal_note Minuto-Rizzo handover '5 January 2004' → '1 January 2004' (and interregnum '~3-week' → '~2-week'); (ii) draft.json::temporal_note Ismay term-start example '4 April 1952' → '24 March 1952'; curation.json::normalization_decisions Term Start/End rule example '4 April 1952' → '24 March 1952'; (iii) draft.json::_extraction_notes Wörner distribution label 'born Stuttgart Weimar Germany 1934' → 'born Stuttgart, Germany per his Wikipedia article's Born field'; curation.json::decision_log Risks/adaptation Wörner label updated to match per-person Born field; curation.json::normalization_decisions per-row Wörner classification 'Stuttgart, Weimar Republic / Württemberg territory (1934)' → 'Stuttgart, Germany (1934) per his Wikipedia article's Born field'; curation.json::normalization_decisions Minuto-Rizzo handover '5 January 2004' → '1 January 2004'; curation.json::open_questions #5 Wörner reframed to acknowledge the modern-state Born-field framing rather than the historical-state framing. Net cycle-1 changes: 6 prose-section accuracy fixes across draft.json and curation.json; no CSV / source_count / row count / schema / metadata / distribution changes (still 13 rows × 4 cols, source_count 14, all CSV cells unchanged).

Post-audit (2026-05-16, cycle 2): cycle-2 verification audit verdict 'Ready+Clean' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Cycle-1 prose-drift fixes confirmed clean: current-state prose now uses '1 January 2004' (Minuto-Rizzo handover), '24 March 1952' (Ismay term-start example), and Wörner's bare 'Stuttgart, Germany' Born-field framing. Old wording remains only in historical cycle-log paragraphs (legitimate). Data state confirmed unchanged: 13 rows × 4 cols, unique Secretary-General PK, chronological term-start ordering 1952-2014, source_count=14, operation_type=join, query_category=implicit_join, claim_type=source_defined, all 13 Birth Country cells grounded by per-person Born fields. NATO master table supports the relevant term dates and acting-row handling; Wörner's page supports the revised birthplace framing. Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-16. Total cycle count: 3 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-2 audit/repair). The instance SATURATES `implicit_join` at 8/8 — NINTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5, factual_lookup 6/5 over-target, top_k 6/5 over-target, multi_hop 5/5, qualitative 5/5. Useful reference: implicit_join instances with master-table-vs-per-person-article cross-references benefit from pre-staging design review to lock in (a) name-normalization rule (per-person Wikipedia article titles for peerage cases), (b) mechanical exclusion clauses (Acting SG '–' marker, incumbent's missing Term End Year), and (c) the modern-sovereign-country birth-country rule (Ismay = India NOT United Kingdom). Compared to Booker/Pulitzer literary-award instances, this NATO instance had a much shorter audit arc (3 cycles vs Booker 4 / Pulitzer 5) because the master-table provenance was simpler (single article-table) and the universe size (13 rows) is smaller.
normalization_decisions:
Universe definition: the staged universe is the 13 numbered permanent NATO Secretaries General with completed terms 1952-2024 per the master 'Secretary General of NATO' Wikipedia article's officeholders table. The universe rule is: 'numbered permanent SG row AND term_end_year IS NOT NULL' — a mechanical 2-clause filter over the master table. The 13 staged SGs in chronological order:
  1. Hastings Ismay, 1st Baron Ismay (1952-1957)
  2. Paul-Henri Spaak (1957-1961)
  3. Dirk Stikker (1961-1964)
  4. Manlio Brosio (1964-1971)
  5. Joseph Luns (1971-1984)
  6. Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington (1984-1988)
  7. Manfred Wörner (1988-1994)
  8. Willy Claes (1994-1995)
  9. Javier Solana (1995-1999)
  10. George Robertson, Baron Robertson of Port Ellen (1999-2003)
  11. Jaap de Hoop Scheffer (2004-2009)
  12. Anders Fogh Rasmussen (2009-2014)
  13. Jens Stoltenberg (2014-2024)

Exclusions:
  - Incumbent Mark Rutte (2024-present, Term End Year unspecified) — excluded by the 'term_end_year IS NOT NULL' clause.
  - Sergio Balanzino, Acting SG between Wörner's death (13 July 1994) and Claes's appointment (17 October 1994) — excluded by the 'numbered permanent' clause (master table marks with '–').
  - Sergio Balanzino, Acting SG between Claes's resignation (October 1995) and Solana's appointment (December 1995) — excluded by the same clause.
  - Alessandro Minuto-Rizzo, Acting SG between Robertson's departure (17 December 2003) and de Hoop Scheffer's appointment (1 January 2004) — excluded by the same clause.

Name normalization rule: 'Secretary-General names use per-person Wikipedia article titles, including peerage forms for ennobled SGs.' Per-row Names:
  - 'Hastings Ismay, 1st Baron Ismay' (per Wikipedia article title; common forms 'Lord Ismay' / 'Hastings Ismay' NOT used)
  - 'Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington' (per article title; common form 'Lord Carrington' NOT used; note 'Carington' single-r in surname vs 'Carrington' double-r in peerage title — both per article)
  - 'George Robertson, Baron Robertson of Port Ellen' (per article title; common form 'George Robertson' NOT used)
  - Other SGs use their full common names per article titles (no peerage): 'Paul-Henri Spaak', 'Dirk Stikker', 'Manlio Brosio', 'Joseph Luns', 'Manfred Wörner' (with diacritic), 'Willy Claes', 'Javier Solana', 'Jaap de Hoop Scheffer', 'Anders Fogh Rasmussen', 'Jens Stoltenberg'.

Term Start Year and Term End Year normalization: integer years extracted from the master NATO table's full-date entries. The master table uses 'D Month YYYY' format (e.g., '24 March 1952 – 16 May 1957' for Ismay). Year extraction takes the integer year component of each date. For Stoltenberg specifically, the master's '1 October 2014 – 1 October 2024' yields Term Start Year = 2014 and Term End Year = 2024 (the tenure was extended from the original 2022 end date due to Russia-Ukraine geopolitical context; staged values reflect the article's actual end date of 1 October 2024).

Birth Country normalization rule: 'Author Birth Country is the modern sovereign country containing the SG's birthplace per the per-person Wikipedia article's Born field. Nationality, country of origin, country of political career, and citizenship are NOT used.' Per-row classifications:
  - Ismay: born Naini Tal, North-Western Provinces, British India (1887) — modern country = India per current sovereign borders of Uttarakhand state. NOT 'United Kingdom' despite his UK military and political career.
  - Spaak: born Schaerbeek, Belgium → 'Belgium'
  - Stikker: born Winschoten, Netherlands → 'Netherlands'
  - Brosio: born Turin, Italy → 'Italy'
  - Luns: born Rotterdam, Netherlands → 'Netherlands'
  - Carrington: born Chelsea, London, England, UK → 'United Kingdom' (constituent-country England → modern sovereign country UK per Booker-precedent rule)
  - Wörner: born Stuttgart, Germany (1934) per his Wikipedia article's Born field — modern sovereign country = Germany. The 1934 historical political state is not used (the staged value follows the Born field's bare 'Stuttgart, Germany' wording).
  - Claes: born Hasselt, Belgium → 'Belgium'
  - Solana: born Madrid, Spain → 'Spain'
  - Robertson: born Port Ellen, Islay, Scotland, UK → 'United Kingdom' (Scotland → UK per constituent-country rule)
  - de Hoop Scheffer: born Amsterdam, Netherlands → 'Netherlands'
  - Rasmussen: born Ginnerup, Denmark → 'Denmark'
  - Stoltenberg: born Oslo, Norway → 'Norway'

Sort order: CSV is sorted by Term Start Year ascending (1952 Ismay → 2014 Stoltenberg), matching the master table's natural chronological order. This is the most-natural sort for an officeholder-succession table.
open_questions: 1. Whether the Ismay row should use 'India' (current staging, per modern-sovereign-country rule) or 'United Kingdom' (per identity/career interpretation) or 'British India' (per historical-political-state-at-time-of-birth). Current modern-sovereign-country rule is consistent with Booker/Pulitzer Lahiri precedent. 2. Whether the SG with peerage names (Ismay/Carrington/Robertson) should use the full peerage form (current staging, per audit-recommended Wikipedia-article-title rule) or shortened display forms ('Lord Ismay' / 'Lord Carrington' / 'George Robertson') for benchmark readability. 3. Whether the 13-row universe should include Rutte with Term End Year = 'Incumbent' as a string sentinel (would break integer-cell evaluability) or current staging excluding Rutte. 4. Whether Acting SGs (Balanzino x2 + Minuto-Rizzo x1) should be included as 3 additional rows with Acting='Yes' flag column (would require schema change to 5 cols) or current exclusion. 5. Whether Wörner's Birth Country 'Germany' (current, per his Wikipedia article's bare 'Stuttgart, Germany' Born field) should be re-keyed to a historical-political-state-at-time-of-birth value (his 1934 birth predates the modern Federal Republic by 15 years); current staging follows the Born field's modern-state framing. 6. Whether the Term End Year for Stoltenberg should be 2022 (original term end before extension) or 2024 (actual term end with extensions; current staging). 7. Whether Carrington's surname spelling 'Carington' (single r) vs 'Carrington' (double r in peerage title) is consistent — the staged 'Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington' preserves both per Wikipedia article title. 8. Whether the entity class should be people/diplomats (current, audit-recommended) or people/politicians (alternative — most NATO SGs are former heads of government / cabinet ministers from member states).
